strings.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
strings.role: Former Myanmar State Counsellor · Democracy politician
strings.summary: After studying abroad, Suu Kyi returned to Myanmar and joined its democracy movement in 1988. Long periods of house arrest accompanied the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize. Following her party’s election win, she became de facto civilian leader in 2016. Her response to the Rohingya crisis and defence of Myanmar at the ICJ drew strong criticism. Detained after the 2021 coup, she spoke with her son in October 2026, he reported; her health remains difficult to verify independently.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long involved in Myanmar’s democracy movement before entering government leadership, her peace-prize reputation, governing controversies and detention have shaped international debate.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Rangoon, then British Burma, now Yangon, Myanmar.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Nonviolent democracy movement
strings.highlights.h1.text: Became a symbol during prolonged detention and received the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BA in philosophy, politics and economics, St Hugh’s College, Oxford (1967).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Government and Rohingya controversy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Her response to the Rohingya crisis and defence of the state drew international criticism during civilian rule.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Phone call with son
strings.timeline.t1.text: Her son confirmed the call to AP, which reported an 18-year sentence under house arrest; health information remained limited.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Detained after coup
strings.timeline.t2.text: The military ousted her government and detained civilian leaders.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Defends Myanmar at ICJ
strings.timeline.t3.text: Led its response to alleged breaches of the Genocide Convention; not a personal criminal trial.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes State Counsellor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became de facto civilian leader while the military retained constitutional powers.
strings.timeline.t5.title: NLD election victory
strings.timeline.t5.text: Her party’s general-election win enabled it to form a government.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t6.text: Honoured for nonviolent struggle for democracy and human rights while detained.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins democracy movement
strings.timeline.t7.text: Returned to Myanmar, joined mass protests and helped establish the NLD.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Oxford degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed her BA in philosophy, politics and economics.
